name: Moore v. Madigan
summary: The Seventh Circuit held that the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms extends beyond the home and struck down Illinois's nearly categorical ban on public carry of ready-to-use firearms.
significance: The Seventh Circuit's decision striking down Illinois's ban on public carry is cited for the proposition that the right to bear arms extends meaningfully outside the home, supporting the petitioners' argument that the public carry right cannot be conditioned on government permission.
